response.markdown_report:
**Selected direction: controlled recency probes for GRU4Rec.** At 0% progress, establish whether recent context helps the supplied model before changing supervision. No improvement is claimed without measurements.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Margins depend on score scale. Pairwise wins complement them but do not estimate HR@10. (2) Feedback motivates recency tests without establishing ownership, incompatibility, or stale preferences. Separate observable dependence from inferred intent. (3) Left padding affects recurrence as well as readout. A zero padding embedding does not prevent GRU state updates.

**Insights from related work.** (1) *Does It Look Sequential?* motivates order controls; *Residual Dominance* motivates preserving the final item. Neither establishes this GRU4Rec’s behavior. (2) Recency Sampling motivates supervision changes after diagnosis. Library documentation requires auditing recurrence before interpreting shortened histories. (3) Krichene–Rendle distinguish sampled ranking from full-catalog evaluation. Cluster bootstrap requires identifiable users, which the supplied loader does not expose.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Controlled variable | Evidence | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| History dependence | Final item, recent context, older content | Paired wins and state changes | Sensitivity does not establish intent |
| Supervision | Training-target recency | Pinned validation HR@10 | Requires retraining |
| Representation geometry | Embedding/state spectrum | Effective rank and variance | Low rank need not harm accuracy |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality / future potential / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Matched history-removal probe — 4/7/5.** Originality: targeted controls improve attribution, but ablations are established. Potential: guides experiments, but training-prefix evidence may not generalize. Difficulty: inference is inexpensive, but padding audits and user pairing require care. References: *Does It Look Sequential?*, *Residual Dominance*, GRU4Rec.
2. **Recency-weighted target sampling — 3/7/4.** Originality: addresses the hypothesis, but follows Recency Sampling. Potential: changes supervision cheaply, but may suppress useful older evidence. Difficulty: small sampler change, but retraining consumes budget.
3. **Spectral health probe — 3/6/2.** Originality: complements cosine similarity, but uses established effective rank. Potential: detects degeneracy, but cannot establish predictive harm. Difficulty: sampled SVD is straightforward, but centering and zero handling matter. References: Guo et al.; Roy–Vetterli.

**Chosen implementation.** Audit baseline recurrence, reset behavior, readout, and predictor consistency first; do not silently substitute padding-free execution. For eligible causal training prefixes, compare original histories, final-item-only input, progressively longer suffixes, matched recent/earlier deletion preserving the final item, and separate final-item deletion. Retain the original oldest-versus-recent deletion comparison as a composite sensitivity test. Fix candidates and perturbation seeds; report paired wins, counts, and state changes separately. Without user IDs, omit bootstrap intervals and label estimates descriptive. With identifiable users, aggregate within user and bootstrap users within categories. Return unavailable values as null with reasons. Preserve required diagnostic interfaces, model mode, four routes, and one checkpoint per category. Prioritize invariant execution checks and prespecified controls to limit diagnostic overinterpretation and validation-driven overfitting.

idea.description: Strengthen the matched history-removal diagnostic with explicit padding audits, final-item controls, reproducible perturbations, and user-aware uncertainty handling for the corrected GRU4Rec baseline.
idea.motivation: The original recent-versus-old deletion comparison changes the immediate predecessor and broader context simultaneously. Padding-dependent recurrence and correlated training observations can further distort interpretation. Controlled probes can guide subsequent experiments without treating qualitative feedback or training-pair wins as measured improvements in held-out HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve view.model as the trained nn.Module and the item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces. Use torch.inference_mode(), temporarily set evaluation mode, and restore the original training flag in finally. Audit explicitly carried recurrent state: eval() does not reset it. Independent histories must start from the model's documented initial state, with no cross-user carryover.

First inspect the supplied implementation when code is available; this report makes no claim that its padding behavior is faulty. Embedding(padding_idx=0) alone does not skip GRU updates. Check repeated-call consistency, batch-order independence, training-side/exported-predictor score agreement, and, where padding updates are intentionally skipped, padding invariance and agreement with unpadded replay. Do not silently change recurrence for diagnosis. If ordinary leading-zero updates make deletion inseparable from padding effects, mark shortened-history results confounded and withhold recency conclusions. Any deliberate padding-free architectural correction must apply consistently to training, ModelView, checkpoint configuration, and the embedded predictor writer, followed by retraining. Internally compact real items chronologically, right-pad, pack with CPU lengths and enforce_sorted=False, then restore B x L features to the original left-padded positions. Never directly pack left-padded inputs. Handle empty histories separately. Gather the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1 in the external left-padded representation.

For up to ten diagnostic batches, choose each row's last position satisfying sequence>0 and positive>0. Retain only nonpadding history through that position, preserving chronological order; keep its positive and negative fixed. Validate both candidate IDs against the real-item range and reject identical candidates. Require at least four retained interactions for matched deletion controls; report eligible and skipped counts by reason. Let n be history length and k=min(3, floor((n-1)/3)). Compare original history; the original composite controls removing k latest or k oldest items; k most recent nonfinal deletions versus k uniformly sampled earlier deletions, always preserving the final item; final-item deletion versus one uniformly sampled earlier deletion; final-item-only history; and suffix lengths 2, 4, 8, 16 and n, clipped to n and deduplicated. For the nonfinal matched control, draw earlier deletions from indices preceding the recent nonfinal block, ensuring disjoint removal regions. Preserve retained-item order, reset state before every replay, and retain the original external sequence width. Use five random-control draws with a local seed-42 generator and deterministic batch/row/variant traversal; average draws within each observation. Record which conditions change the final item. Optional prefix shuffling fixes the final item and complements deletion controls because it preserves history length; robustness to it does not exclude unordered prefix dependence.

For fixed positive and negative candidates, pairwise win is 1 for a positive win, 0 for a loss, and 0.5 for a tie. Report intervention-minus-original mean wins and direct paired differences between matched conditions, together with raw original/intervention means, counts, and separately reported 1-cosine state distances. Flag zero-norm states and exclude them only from cosine summaries. Retain existing sampled-margin and embedding-geometry diagnostics, clearly identifying their scale and interpretation limits. Category metadata is unavailable: retain empty category breakdowns with an explicit unavailable reason. Do not use review fields, item ratings, categories, prices, stores, or inferred simulator traits. Titles, descriptions, timestamps, and interaction histories are the only permitted contextual evidence.

The loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), so it supplies no reliable user IDs. Do not infer IDs from matching histories or bootstrap rows as independent users. Loader-based aggregates are descriptive and may weight frequent users more heavily. User uncertainty intervals require a separately constructed, explicitly user-indexed training-history sample using user_train, with causal held-out-within-training prefixes and candidates sampled only from permitted data; disclose that changed diagnostic sampling protocol. Average repeated observations within each user, bootstrap users independently within each category using the same resampled indices for all conditions, use 2,000 replicates with seed 42, and average category differences equally. Report percentile 95% intervals only when all four category summaries are available. These intervals condition on fixed trained checkpoints and candidates and omit training-seed uncertainty. If reliable IDs or four-category observations are absent, return null intervals with reasons.

These probes are training-prefix sensitivity diagnostics, not HR@10, evidence of user intent, or proof of a last-item shortcut. Greater damage from deleting the final item establishes sensitivity; judging harmful shortcut use also requires controlled held-out predictive evidence. Keep pinned validation users, targets, candidates, and evaluator unchanged; selection remains macro validation HR@10. Prespecify a small diagnostic panel and subsequent training hypotheses, log all attempted trials, and avoid repeatedly tuning to the same 800 validation users. No hidden test data, external datasets, or pretrained weights are used. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Use one independently trained checkpoint per category without fusion. Frozen diagnostic variants are interventions on that same model, not additional predictors.
idea.pseudocode:
audit actual GRU recurrence, initial state, readout, ModelView, and predictor writer
record execution checks and any padding-dependent confounding
save model.training
try:
    model.eval()
    with inference_mode():
        for first 10 batches (_, seq, pos, neg), in deterministic order:
            for each row:
                t = maximum index where seq != 0 and pos != 0
                if no t: record skip; continue
                history = nonzero(seq[:t+1]) in original order
                target, candidate = pos[t], neg[t]
                validate history and real, distinct candidate IDs
                if len(history) < 4: record skip; continue
                k = min(3, (len(history)-1)//3)
                construct original, composite recent/old deletion controls
                construct recent-nonfinal deletion preserving final item
                draw 5 matched earlier-deletion controls from disjoint earlier region
                construct final deletion and 5 single-earlier-deletion controls
                construct final-only and deduplicated suffix-length controls
                optionally construct fixed-final prefix shuffles
                for each variant:
                    x = left_pad_to_original_width(retained_history)
                    reset explicit recurrent state using audited model contract
                    features = view.log2feats(x)
                    state = features[maximum_nonpadding_index(x)]
                    scores = view.predict_score(state, fixed_target_and_candidate)
                    record tie-aware win and valid state cosine distance
                average random draws within observation
                record paired differences and final-item-preservation flags
    aggregate descriptive statistics with counts and confounding flags
    if reliable user-indexed observations exist for all four categories:
        average observations within user
        bootstrap users within category, paired across conditions
        macro-average four category differences equally
        report 2000-replicate percentile intervals, seed 42
    else:
        intervals = null with explicit reason
    return {metrics, metric_definitions}
finally:
    model.train(saved_training_flag)

interpreter_prompt(raw):
    embed measured metrics, definitions, counts, and execution-audit findings
    distinguish composite deletion, final-item dependence, and broader context sensitivity
    describe training-pair results separately from pinned validation HR@10
    prohibit unsupported intent, ownership, compatibility, shortcut, or improvement claims

originality.positive: Combines final-item controls, matched context deletion, and execution audits within the family-specific diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: The underlying ablation, pairing, and bootstrap methods are established; the contribution is primarily a careful diagnostic integration.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish several competing explanations and support more focused recency-sampling or recurrent-state experiments.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix sensitivity may not generalize to held-out HR@10, and diagnostic refinement alone does not improve recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: Most probes reuse frozen-model inference and require no additional trained model.
code_difficulty.negative: Auditing recurrent state, maintaining predictor consistency, implementing matched perturbations, and obtaining reliable user-indexed uncertainty require more work than the original rating suggested.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Studies sequential structure through interaction shuffling, accuracy changes, and recommendation overlap across 15 datasets.
Motivates comparing predictive effects separately from recommendation-list sensitivity.
limitations: Full-history shuffling changes the final item and earlier order together.
Reported findings do not establish outcomes on these four Amazon datasets.

related_work.title: Residual Dominance
contributions: Provides fixed-final-item prefix-shuffling controls that motivate separating immediate-predecessor dependence from earlier-order dependence.
limitations: The reported Transformer residual mechanism should not be assumed to explain GRU4Rec.
Prefix-shuffle robustness does not exclude dependence on unordered prefix content.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Investigates recency-oriented training sampling for recurrent recommendation.
limitations: Does not establish stale-history failures or expected improvement under this task's pinned metric.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking evaluation can change model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not justify replacing the fixed selection protocol.
One-negative pairwise accuracy is not an estimate of the task's HR@10.

related_work.title: GRU4Rec official implementation
contributions: Provides recurrent session-recommendation methods and implementation context.
limitations: Session assumptions require care for longer user histories.
Its implementation does not establish the supplied host model's padding or state-reset behavior.

related_work.title: Guo et al., ICML 2024
contributions: Studies low-dimensional embedding collapse in recommendation.
limitations: Low effective rank alone does not establish harmful collapse in the supplied GRU4Rec.

related_work.title: The Effective Rank: A Measure of Effective Dimensionality
contributions: Defines an entropy-based summary of singular-value spectra.
limitations: Measures representation geometry rather than recommendation quality.
Zero spectra require explicit handling.

related_work.title: PyTorch Embedding documentation
contributions: Documents padding_idx behavior for embedding entries.
limitations: A fixed zero padding embedding does not mask downstream recurrent updates.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Documents recurrent equations and zero initialization when an initial state is omitted.
limitations: Evaluation mode does not reset application-managed recurrent state.
Library semantics do not establish the host implementation's behavior.

related_work.title: PyTorch pack_padded_sequence documentation
contributions: Documents sequence packing, CPU length requirements, and enforce_sorted behavior.
limitations: Direct packing of left-padded histories retains leading padding and can truncate real items.

related_work.title: PyTorch pad_packed_sequence documentation
contributions: Documents restoration of packed sequence outputs.
limitations: External left-padded feature alignment must still be restored explicitly when required by ModelView.

related_work.title: Cluster-bootstrap methods
contributions: Supports resampling whole clusters when repeated observations are dependent.
limitations: Requires reliable cluster identifiers.
User bootstrap intervals do not capture training-seed uncertainty.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling that preserves correspondence between conditions.
limitations: Pairing alone does not account for multiple correlated observations per user; user-level aggregation or cluster resampling is required.
